title: Preparing the Soil Is Not Remembering the Exposure: A Gated Test Plan for EV-Associated Effects
content: Tumour extracellular vesicles (EVs) can prepare distant tissue for tumour cells in animal models. That is a claim about tissue. Whether exposed cells keep a lasting phenotype, and whether their daughters inherit it, are separate claims that need their own proof. Here I set out three testable hypotheses and a four-gate framework for the cell-level claims. H1: EVs add a measurable share to tissue priming. H2: an exposed cell keeps a pre-defined phenotype after exposure ends. H3: daughter cells carry it. For each, I state what would support it, what would count against it, and what would leave it open. A label system (P, M, H) grades the evidence for a claim, not the cell. The aim is to stop a tissue result from being read, step by step and unnoticed, as cell memory or inheritance. No new data are reported.
